title: Psalms Chapter 36 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 36 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 36 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 36.

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:1, what does the transgression of the wicked say within the psalmist's heart?
options: There is no fear of God before his eyes
questions.correctAnswer: There is no fear of God before his eyes
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:1 states that the transgression of the wicked saith within the heart that there is no fear of God before his eyes.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 36:2 says that the wicked flattereth himself in his own eyes until his iniquity is found to be hateful.
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:2 clearly states the wicked flattereth himself in his own eyes, until his iniquity be found to be hateful.

questions.question: What are the words of the wicked described as in Psalms 36:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:3 says the words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit.

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:4, what does the wicked devise upon his bed?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:4 states that he deviseth mischief upon his bed.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 36:4 describes the wicked as abhorreth not evil.
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:4 says the wicked abhorreth not evil.

questions.question: In Psalms 36:1, who is identified as the author of this Psalm?
questions.explanation: The heading in Psalms 36:1 states this is a Psalm of David the servant of the LORD.

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:3, what has the wicked left off doing?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:3 states he hath left off to be wise, and to do good.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 36:2 says the wicked is humble in his own eyes.
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:2 says the wicked flattereth himself in his own eyes, not that he is humble.

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:4, the wicked setteth himself in what kind of way?
options: A way that is not good
questions.correctAnswer: A way that is not good
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:4 says he setteth himself in a way that is not good.

questions.question: Which of the following comes first in Psalms 36?
options: The wicked deviseth mischief upon his bed
The transgression of the wicked saith within my heart there is no fear of God
The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit
Thy mercy, O LORD, is in the heavens
questions.correctAnswer: The transgression of the wicked saith within my heart there is no fear of God
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:1 starts with the transgression of the wicked saying there is no fear of God, which comes before the other listed verses.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 36:1 is addressed 'To the chief Musician'.
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:1 begins with 'To the chief Musician'.

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:3, what has the wicked's mouth ceased to do?
options: To be wise and to do good
questions.correctAnswer: To be wise and to do good
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:3 states he hath left off to be wise, and to do good.

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:2, until when does the wicked flatter himself in his own eyes?
options: Until his iniquity be found to be hateful
questions.correctAnswer: Until his iniquity be found to be hateful
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:2 says the wicked flattereth himself in his own eyes, until his iniquity be found to be hateful.

questions.question: What does the wicked not abhor, according to Psalms 36:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:4 says the wicked abhorreth not evil.

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:1, who is described as having no fear of God before his eyes?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:1 says the transgression of the wicked saith there is no fear of God before his eyes.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 36 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 36 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:5, where is the LORD's mercy described to be?
options: In the hearts of the faithful
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:5 says, 'Thy mercy, O LORD, is in the heavens; and thy faithfulness reacheth unto the clouds,' showing that God's mercy is exalted and vast, reaching the heavens and clouds.

questions.question: How does Psalms 36:6 describe God's righteousness and judgments?
options: Like the ocean waves and the sky
Like the great mountains and a great deep
Like the desert sands and the stars
Like a gentle breeze and a calm sea
questions.correctAnswer: Like the great mountains and a great deep
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:6 states, 'Thy righteousness is like the great mountains; thy judgments are a great deep,' emphasizing the immensity and stability of God's character and decisions.

questions.question: What does Psalms 36:7 teach about the reason people trust in God?
options: Because of His power in battle
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'How excellent is thy lovingkindness, O God! therefore the children of men put their trust under the shadow of thy wings,' which connects God's lovingkindness as the foundation for human trust.

questions.question: In Psalms 36:8, what kind of satisfaction does God provide to those who trust Him?
options: Abundant satisfaction with the fatness of His house and the river of His pleasures
questions.correctAnswer: Abundant satisfaction with the fatness of His house and the river of His pleasures
questions.explanation: The verse describes God’s provision as abundant satisfaction through 'the fatness of thy house' and 'the river of thy pleasures,' indicating deep and lasting spiritual nourishment.

questions.question: How does Psalms 36:9 connect the concept of life to God's presence?
options: Life is found in earthly treasures
Life is found in the absence of trouble
Life is found with God as the fountain and in His light
Life is found through human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Life is found with God as the fountain and in His light
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:9 states, 'For with thee is the fountain of life: in thy light shall we see light,' linking true life and understanding directly to God's presence and illumination.

questions.question: What does Psalms 36:10 ask God to continue toward those who know Him?
questions.explanation: The verse petitions, 'O continue thy lovingkindness unto them that know thee; and thy righteousness to the upright in heart,' emphasizing ongoing grace and justice for the faithful.

questions.question: What practical lesson about humility and pride is taught in Psalms 36:11?
options: Pride should be embraced to gain respect
Avoid the foot of pride and the hand of the wicked to maintain safety
Pride is a sign of strength
questions.correctAnswer: Avoid the foot of pride and the hand of the wicked to maintain safety
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:11 says, 'Let not the foot of pride come against me, and let not the hand of the wicked remove me,' teaching believers to seek humility and protection from evil influences.

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:12, what is the fate of the workers of iniquity?
options: They shall be cast down and not able to rise
They will be honored among men
They will be forgiven without repentance
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be cast down and not able to rise
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states, 'There are the workers of iniquity fallen: they are cast down, and shall not be able to rise,' indicating the downfall of the wicked is final and irreversible.

questions.question: What does Psalms 36:7 teach us about trust in God in times of trouble?
options: Trusting in God is a sign of weakness
Trusting in God provides protection under His wings
Trusting in God guarantees no hardship
Trusting in God means ignoring problems
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting in God provides protection under His wings
questions.explanation: The verse depicts those who trust God as finding refuge 'under the shadow of thy wings,' symbolizing protection and care during adversity.

questions.question: How do Psalms 36:5 and 36:6 together describe God's character?
options: Faithful, merciful, righteous, and just with great reach and depth
questions.correctAnswer: Faithful, merciful, righteous, and just with great reach and depth
questions.explanation: Verse 5 describes God's mercy and faithfulness reaching the heavens and clouds, while verse 6 likens His righteousness and judgments to great mountains and deep waters, illustrating His vast and perfect character.

questions.question: What promise does Psalms 36:8 give to those who trust in God, based on His 'house' and 'river' imagery?
options: They shall be abundantly satisfied and delighted
They will gain wealth and fame
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be abundantly satisfied and delighted
questions.explanation: The verse promises abundant satisfaction 'with the fatness of thy house' and drinking 'of the river of thy pleasures,' indicating spiritual fullness and joy for believers.

questions.question: A believer feels overwhelmed by fear and doubt. According to Psalms 36:7-8, what truth should encourage them?
options: They must rely only on their own strength
God’s lovingkindness offers protection and abundant satisfaction
They should avoid trusting God in hard times
They will face punishment for their doubts
questions.correctAnswer: God’s lovingkindness offers protection and abundant satisfaction
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 teach that God's excellent lovingkindness provides refuge 'under the shadow of thy wings' and satisfies with the riches of His house and pleasures, encouraging trust in God during fear.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 36:9 teaches that light comes from God and through Him we see light.
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:9 explicitly states, 'For with thee is the fountain of life: in thy light shall we see light,' confirming that God is the source of life and illumination.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 36:11, pride is welcomed as a positive attribute for the psalmist.
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:11 states, 'Let not the foot of pride come against me,' showing the psalmist’s desire to avoid pride, not embrace it.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 36:10 encourages God to continue His lovingkindness and righteousness toward the upright in heart.
questions.explanation: The verse prays, 'O continue thy lovingkindness unto them that know thee; and thy righteousness to the upright in heart,' affirming God's ongoing grace and justice towards the faithful.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 36 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 36.

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:9, what is described as the 'fountain of life'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:9 states 'For with thee is the fountain of life', referring directly to the LORD as the source of life.

questions.question: In Psalms 36:10, to whom does the psalmist ask God to continue His lovingkindness?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:10 requests God to continue His lovingkindness to 'them that know thee', indicating the faithful.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God to prevent in Psalms 36:11?
options: The foot of pride coming against him
The hand of the wicked removing him
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:11 explicitly asks, 'Let not the foot of pride come against me, and let not the hand of the wicked remove me.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:12, what is the fate of the workers of iniquity?
options: They have fallen and cannot rise
questions.correctAnswer: They have fallen and cannot rise
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:12 declares that the workers of iniquity 'are cast down, and shall not be able to rise.'

questions.question: The phrase 'in thy light shall we see light' in Psalms 36:9 is an example of which literary device?
questions.explanation: The structure 'in thy light shall we see light' reflects a chiastic pattern, where the concept of light is mirrored for emphasis (Psalms 36:9).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God as the source of life, similar to Psalms 36:9?
questions.explanation: John 1:4 states, 'In him was life; and the life was the light of men,' echoing the theme in Psalms 36:9 of God as the fountain of life and light.

questions.question: What Hebrew word, meaning 'lovingkindness,' is significant in Psalms 36:7 and 10, illustrating God's covenant faithfulness?
questions.explanation: 'Chesed' is the Hebrew term translated as 'lovingkindness' and highlights God's steadfast love and covenant faithfulness in Psalms 36:7 and 36:10.

questions.question: How does Psalms 36:8 use metaphor to describe God's provision for His people?
options: As a river of pleasures and a fat house satisfying them
As a lamp lighting their path
As a shepherd guiding his sheep
questions.correctAnswer: As a river of pleasures and a fat house satisfying them
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:8 uses metaphor to depict God's provision as 'the fatness of thy house' and 'the river of thy pleasures', symbolizing abundance and joy.

questions.question: The plea in Psalms 36:11 to prevent the 'foot of pride' and 'hand of the wicked' from harming the psalmist reflects what common biblical theme?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:11 reflects the biblical theme of God protecting the righteous from the harm caused by prideful and wicked enemies.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage also emphasizes the righteous finding refuge under God's protection, similar to Psalms 36:7?
questions.explanation: Psalm 91:4 speaks of God covering the righteous 'under his wings', paralleling Psalms 36:7's imagery of trust under God's wings.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 36:12 indicates that the workers of iniquity will rise again after their fall.
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:12 states, 'They are cast down, and shall not be able to rise,' indicating the workers of iniquity cannot rise again.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 36:5 portrays God's mercy and faithfulness as reaching to the heavens and clouds.
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:5 says, 'Thy mercy, O LORD, is in the heavens; and thy faithfulness reacheth unto the clouds,' affirming this imagery.

questions.question: How does Psalms 36:6 describe the righteousness and judgments of God?
options: Like the shifting sands and shallow waters
Like the great mountains and a great deep
Like the wind and the fire
Like the stars and the moon
questions.correctAnswer: Like the great mountains and a great deep
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:6 compares God's righteousness to 'the great mountains' and His judgments to 'a great deep', emphasizing their stability and profundity.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse reflects the theme of seeing light through God's light as in Psalms 36:9?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:8 says, 'For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord,' echoing Psalms 36:9's theme of illumination through God's light.

questions.question: What is the primary historical and cultural context for the warnings against pride and wickedness in Psalms 36:11?
options: Ancient Near Eastern kingship and social injustice
questions.correctAnswer: Ancient Near Eastern kingship and social injustice
questions.explanation: The warnings in Psalms 36:11 reflect the context of Ancient Near Eastern culture where prideful rulers often oppressed the innocent, a social injustice addressed in Hebrew poetry.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 36 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 36 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 36:1 reveal about the wicked's mindset?
options: They are aware of their sin
They have no fear of God
questions.correctAnswer: They have no fear of God
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:1 states that the transgression of the wicked indicates there is no fear of God before his eyes, highlighting their disregard for divine authority.

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:3, what has the wicked ceased to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:3 indicates that the wicked have left off to be wise and to do good, demonstrating their moral decline.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 36:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:5 emphasizes God's mercy, stating it is in the heavens, showcasing His boundless grace toward humanity.

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Psalms 36:7 to describe God's protection?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:7 states that the children of men put their trust under the shadow of God's wings, symbolizing His protective care.

questions.question: In Psalms 36:9, what does the psalmist say is found with God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:9 describes God as the source of life, indicating that true spiritual vitality comes from Him.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 5 and 6 convey about God's nature?
options: God is merciful but also just
God is only concerned with judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God is merciful but also just
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 together show God's mercy in the heavens and judgment that reaches deep, balancing His compassion with His righteousness.

questions.question: What does Psalms 36:11 request regarding pride and wickedness?
options: To be removed from the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:11 expresses a plea for protection from the foot of pride and the hand of the wicked, indicating a desire for deliverance from oppression.

questions.question: According to Psalms 36:8, what will those who trust in God experience?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:8 promises that those who trust in God's lovingkindness will be abundantly satisfied, reflecting His provision and care.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 36:10 suggest about God's relationship with the upright?
options: God extends lovingkindness to the upright
God is indifferent to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God extends lovingkindness to the upright
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:10 highlights that God's lovingkindness is directed toward those who know Him and are upright in heart, indicating His relational nature.

questions.question: What does Psalms 36:12 indicate about the fate of the workers of iniquity?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:12 states that the workers of iniquity have fallen and shall not be able to rise, demonstrating the ultimate consequence of their actions.

questions.question: How does Psalms 36:4 describe the wicked's behavior at night?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:4 reveals that the wicked devise mischief upon their bed, indicating premeditated evil intentions.

questions.question: What aspect of God's character is exemplified in Psalms 36:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:6 exemplifies God's righteousness, comparing it to great mountains, which indicates its strength and stability.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that God is indifferent to human suffering. What does Psalms 36:5-6 actually teach?
options: God does not care about humanity
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:5-6 teaches that God's mercy is in the heavens and His righteousness is like great mountains, showing He is actively involved in caring for humanity.

questions.question: What do Psalms 36:2 and 3 reveal about the self-perception of the wicked?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:2 says the wicked flatter themselves until their iniquity is found to be hateful, indicating a distorted self-image.

questions.question: What is the ultimate source of light according to Psalms 36:9?
questions.explanation: Psalms 36:9 declares that with God is the fountain of life and in His light, we see light, affirming Him as the ultimate source of spiritual illumination.
